vehicleUpdates.summary: Strong mixed-facing three-across evidence in a related 2021 Grande, with useful rear-facing front clearance. GX shares the generation but lacks some Grande equipment. Third-row child-restraint use and access need particular care.

battery.basis: Calculated nominal NiMH energy: 288 V × 6.5 Ah = 1.872 kWh, rounded. Original and updated Toyota hybrid manuals agree; this is not usable capacity or a plug-in battery.

observedConsumption.basis: AAA observed petrol use: exact GX AWD AXUH78R, May 2023 build, 16,925 km; 93 km Geelong route, 8–10 July 2024, 95 RON. Not a guarantee for all loads, routes or model years. Official ADR combined remains 5.6.

consumption.basis: Official Australian ADR 81/02 combined GX hybrid claim; separate AAA observed result is 5.8.

boot.basis: Toyota cargo capacity with third row folded, second row upright; not an all-seven-seats figure.

bootAllRows.basis: Toyota cargo capacity with all three rows upright.

towing.basis: Maximum braked trailer capacity; actual towbar, load and vehicle limits apply.

familyFit.summary: Related Grande test demonstrated three across including rear-facing Attain More; GX still needs your exact fit check. ANCAP found a different rear-facing ISOFIX seat incompatible.
familyFit.row2: Three seatback top tethers; outboard ISOFIX only. ANCAP reports one tested rear-facing convertible could not use outboard ISOFIX; an outboard belt-installed capsule required care.
familyFit.row3: No top tether or ISOFIX. ANCAP recommends against installing child restraints here; do not count row 3 as an extra position for this family’s mixed three-seat arrangement.
familyFit.testedSeats: 2021 Grande: Aspire More booster plus two Attain More seats, tested in forward- and rear-facing modes. Front clearance was demonstrated with a rear-facing Attain More and a 180 cm driver. Exact mixed positions are not fully mapped in text.
familyFit.buckleAccess: No verified test of independent booster fastening with three installed. The owner manual warns adjacent belts may interfere with some restraints. Trial buckles with your actual seats.
familyFit.access: BabyDrive found a child-sized third-row gap after sliding an ISOFIX-occupied row-2 seat. Toyota manuals warn never to adjust the vehicle seat after securing the restraint. Do not rely on that shortcut; check the exact manual and trial entry with seats correctly installed.
familyFit.ventilation: GX Hybrid had three-zone climate from launch, confirmed by its own GX road test; the related Grande family test confirms ceiling outlets in both rear rows. Grande sunblinds and 360-degree camera are not GX equipment.

pros: Related mixed-facing three-across test, with a 180 cm driver ahead of the rear-facing seat.
GX Hybrid has three-zone climate; boot remains 241 L with all rows upright.
Exact GX AAA test returned 5.8 L/100 km on 95 RON.
cons: Third row has no restraint anchors and is not an assumed child-seat solution.
Three-across booster buckle access remains unverified.
Large parking footprint; early GX equipment differs from 2026 cars.
inspection: Check the VIN against current official recall campaigns; this dataset is not a complete recall history.
Confirm battery-health checks and remaining Toyota warranty eligibility.
Trial your pram with the third row in the intended position.
Check current GX ventilation and safety/multimedia equipment rather than relying on Grande photos.
Original 2021 Australian hybrid launch and current February 2026 sheet both specify minimum 95 RON premium unleaded; budget the matching fuel grade.

The three captured GX Hybrid VINs are listed in REC-006562 second-row recliner campaign data. Obtain completion evidence; neither the model year nor the advert establishes that the free remedy has been carried out.
Install all three actual restraints, including the rear-facing one; try the front seats in both adults’ driving positions and check booster buckle reach.
Check the Australian restraint/vehicle manuals together. A different rear-facing convertible failed ANCAP outboard ISOFIX installation; a seatbelt route may differ.
Ask Toyota for all outstanding VIN campaigns and completed repair orders, including the September 2026 expansion of second-row recliner campaign 6GG11.
Check hybrid battery cooling-intake cleanliness, warning history, battery-health records and remaining conditional cover.
Ask for the next several VIN-specific service quotes, including spark plugs, coolant and brake-fluid work when due. A launch capped service price does not cover indefinite aged-car maintenance.

changes.text: Australian XU70 hybrid introduced with 2.5L eFour AWD, 184 kW combined and GX three-zone climate. Do not apply V6-petrol fuel, service or driveline details to the hybrid.

Hybrid drivetrain retained. GX driver display grew from 4.2 to 7 inches; updated multimedia added wireless Apple CarPlay and Connected Services. The 12.3-inch centre screen belonged to GXL/Grande, not GX.
Toyota ended petrol-only Kluger orders. Existing used petrol cars remain a different powertrain; this record covers GX AWD Hybrid only.

Lists a 12.3-inch driver information display, tyre-pressure monitoring and USB-C ports across grades, while GX retains an 8-inch centre touchscreen. Confirm build/equipment; these features must not be back-applied to 2021–22 asking samples.

gaps: Named three-seat test is a related Grande, not a direct GX test of every year or your restraints. Independent three-across booster fastening is not established.
2021–22 used asking sample does not value every year through 2026. The February 2026 sheet has material equipment changes; confirm production applicability by VIN.
Exact post-cap service schedule prices and fitted AXUH78R replacement-pack cost remain unverified. Nominal battery energy is known; usable battery energy is not.

length.basis: Toyota overall body length; original/current XU70 hybrid specifications.

width.basis: Toyota body width, excluding mirrors. Body width alone does not establish three-restraint fit.

safety.applicability: ANCAP report covers all XU7 petrol/hybrid variants built from March 2021, on sale June 2021; curtain protection covers all three rows. Child installation assessment is per position, not three-across.

priceUpdates.geography: Queensland · three distinct GX Hybrid AWD dealer-used cars
priceUpdates.note: Three distinct Queensland 2021–22 GX Hybrid AWD asking ads; median A$48,490. Current raw public dealer HTML verifies Booval A$48,490/47,122 km and Gympie A$49,990/12,181 km; indexed dealer text is stale. The 12,181–106,500 km spread is material. This used sample does not value new 2025–26 GX stock, separately observed at A$64,990–67,250 drive-away.
priceUpdates.estimateBasis: Current, physically distinct asking-price sample, not achieved sale prices or a value for every grouped year. Dealer stock/VINs prevent double counting; confirm availability and the buyer-specific drive-away amount.

observations.note: Current dealer stock 15437; VIN 5TDLB3CH00S058648 confirms GX Hybrid AWD. Dealer list labels fuel generically Petrol but its 2.5L hybrid VIN/specification is cross-checked; 3.5L petrol stock 15355 is excluded. This exact VIN is present in official REC-006562 second-row recliner recall data; completion is unknown. Request Toyota remedy paperwork.

Stock U675461; VIN 5TDLB3CH80S101780; rego 004QM2. Current raw public HTML/structured offer and odometer are A$48,490 DAP/47,122 km, overriding cached A$49,880/47,104 km. Toyota-certified claims and campaign completion need documentation. This VIN was already matched to official recliner recall data; remedy completion remains unknown.

Stock U13155; GX Hybrid AXUH78R; Graphite. Current public dealer HTML/structured offer verifies A$49,990 DAP and 12,181 km. Counted once across dealer-group cross-posts. This VIN was already matched to official recliner recall data; obtain completion evidence.

fuelEstimate.basis: L/100 km petrol planning anchor from AAA’s exact 2023 GX AWD test: 5.8 overall. The 5.5–7.5 sensitivity band is assumed, informed by AAA segment results and CarExpert short urban use around 7.0; it is not a fleet-average interval. Extrapolation to the grouped 2021–26 drivetrain remains an estimate. Uses 95 RON.

ownershipUpdates.serviceBasis: ESTIMATE — A$500/year at 15,000 km/year, A$300–700 sensitivity. Original 2021 launch offered A$250 standard scheduled visits during the first five years/75,000 km; this is historical eligibility, not a fresh cap for a used purchase. Later service prices require the VIN, mileage and service number. Parts, labour and scheduled fluids belong to standard servicing; extra severe-use work and wear items are separate. No verified post-cap ten-year average was found.

risks.title: Hybrid battery outside cover
risks.detail: A traction-battery fault needs diagnosis before replacement. Infinitev lists a 2021-on AXUH78 replacement but no public fitted price; obtain a VIN-specific quote and warranty terms. The retained A$4,500–9,000 scenario is a RAV4-based planning analogue, not a Kluger quotation or expected failure bill.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE — A$4,500–9,000 fitted new-genuine pack planning scenario, assuming labour and GST. Analogue: Australian 2019-on RAV4 guide A$4,500–7,000 fitted, with up to A$2,000 extra uncertainty for Kluger pack/sourcing; guide GST unspecified. No verified AXUH78R quote or compatible part is claimed.
risks.warranty: Confirm annual extended-cover eligibility before funding a repair; normal capacity degradation is excluded.

risks.title: Second-row seat-frame recall
risks.detail: Campaign ZGGA0 affects selected 2021–2024 Kluger petrol/hybrid vehicles: a seat-frame bar can protrude with the bench partly stowed.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for the official VIN-specific recall remedy, including dealer installation; not a replacement-seat price.
risks.warranty: Free rear-protector installation for affected VINs.

risks.title: Driver-airbag spiral-cable recall
risks.detail: Selected March–July 2023 production can lose the driver-airbag circuit connection. Verify inspection and any required cable replacement.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for Toyota’s VIN-specific recall inspection/replacement, including dealer work; unrelated airbag faults need diagnosis.
risks.warranty: Official serial-number inspection and necessary replacement are free for involved VINs.

risks.title: 2022–2025 combination-meter recall
risks.detail: REC-006390 (campaign 5GG31) includes selected RAV4 Hybrid and Kluger Hybrid VINs. A memory/software issue can blank the meter, hiding speed and warning indicators. The published notice anticipated a late-2025 software remedy; confirm its current availability and completion with Toyota. Do not apply automatically to the new-generation 2026 RAV4.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for the official VIN-applicable recall remedy. This is rectification of an identified campaign, not a future owner-paid replacement quote.
risks.warranty: Check the VIN and campaign completion with the Australian manufacturer; official recall rectification is separate from ordinary warranty expiry.

risks.title: Second-row recliner recall — separate from frame protector
risks.detail: REC-006562 / 6GG11 was expanded on 24 September 2026 to 46,467 Australian Klugers produced 31 March 2021–10 June 2025, including selected GX hybrids. The row-2 seatback can move if its recliner fails to engage. Toyota replaces return springs free for affected VINs. Confirm completion independently of the older seat-frame protector campaign.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for the official VIN-applicable recall remedy. This is rectification of an identified campaign, not a future owner-paid replacement quote.
risks.warranty: Check the VIN and campaign completion with the Australian manufacturer; official recall rectification is separate from ordinary warranty expiry.

risks.title: Additional early Kluger safety campaigns
risks.detail: Selected 2021 cars have front-seat frame/ADR rectification (REC-005459); selected 2021–2023 cars need improved lower-bumper fasteners (REC-005813). Selected March 2021–April 2022 hybrid builds also have VSC reset software rectification. Check completion by VIN rather than inferring from model year.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for the official VIN-applicable recall remedy. This is rectification of an identified campaign, not a future owner-paid replacement quote.
risks.warranty: Check the VIN and campaign completion with the Australian manufacturer; official recall rectification is separate from ordinary warranty expiry.

reviewUpdates.scope: ProductReview AWD Hybrid 2021–26 page, seven GX/GXL/Grande posts. One is labelled Fair Incentive. Excludes the 3.8/5 broad Kluger parent aggregate and pre-2021 petrol generations; it is not a representative reliability survey.
reviewUpdates.summary: Seven self-selected AWD Hybrid posts average 3.0/5. Positives concern room, smoothness and economy; negatives include trim/seals, equipment and isolated warranty handling. Several Grande-specific issues do not apply directly to GX, and the sample does not measure failure rates.
positiveThemes: Roomy cabin and smooth, quiet driving
Economy praised against previous large family cars
negativeThemes: Lane-assist intrusiveness and a sunroof creak in one report
Individual dissatisfaction with warranty handling and equipment

insuranceUpdates.basis: NRMA August 2026 Kluger GX Hybrid study lists A$8,111 comprehensive insurance over five years; annualised A$1,622.20, rounded to A$1,620. Reference: 30-year-old man, Chatswood NSW, private use, clean history, A$1,000 excess; prices correct 30 June 2026. This is an arithmetic study average, not a Queensland annual quote or guaranteed renewals. Youi all-Kluger mean A$1,433 and A$907–1,839 band pool years/powertrains and provide context only. Comprehensive cover only; CTP is separately included in registration. The budget and low/high bounds are household planning assumptions, not a personalised quote, insurer minimum/maximum or confidence interval. Address, drivers, excess, insured value and cover can change the premium. Replace with a like-for-like current quote; no arbitrary SUV or generation multiplier is applied.
insuranceUpdates.scope: NSW GX Hybrid study · annualised five-year cost

tyreUpdates.basis: Budget aftermarket fitted-set estimate, not a retailer quote. Tempe NSW lists Nexen Roadian GTX 106V A$185 each / A$740 four fitted on sale and Yokohama G058 106V A$195 each / A$780 four fitted. A$900 allows Queensland fitting/freight variation. These interstate prices are not a Brisbane quote; confirm GST, inclusions and local stock. A cheaper local Rapid listing was sold out and was not treated as an available four-tyre offer. Life is a common 40,000 km planning assumption (25,000–60,000 km sensitivity), not a measured model or tyre average. Wear varies with tyre choice, driving, maintenance and vehicle; model-specific replacement averages were not verified. Annual allowance = set budget × annual km ÷ 40,000, rounded to A$10. Age/damage can require earlier replacement. Alignment is additional; actual placard, wheel package and local fitted quote must be checked. Matching size/load/speed does not establish equal braking, efficiency or durability.

repairReserveUpdates.basis: A$800/year savings allowance, assumed A$400–1,600 range, for grouped used large AWD hybrids with differing age and remaining cover. No public Australian AXUH78R fleet repair-spend or failure-frequency dataset was found. Recall remedies are free; battery replacement is a separate low-confidence stress case, and scheduled servicing/tyres/insured collision damage are excluded. Conditional battery/driveline cover can reduce owner-paid exposure. Exact fitted pack and major component prices remain quote-only; this is not an empirical expected repair bill.

fitAssessments.summary: Strong named mixed-facing test in a related 2021 Grande; retain GX and rear-facing compatibility checks. No booster-buckle confirmation or approved extra tethered row-3 positions.

arrangement.detail: Grande test fitted Aspire More booster plus two Attain More seats in rear/forward modes. This supports the mixed-facing target but does not prove all seat models or each position; ANCAP could not correctly install one other convertible rear-facing with outboard ISOFIX. Three GX row-2 tethers are documented.

buckles.detail: No demonstrated independent fastening with three installed. Toyota warns some restraints interfere with adjacent belts. Check actual booster buckle reach.

space.detail: BabyDrive reports a 180 cm driver ahead of rear-facing Attain More while a 162 cm tester could also occupy row 3. Its named seat and related Grande scope matter; exact GX front-seat position still needs a trial.

access.detail: Published third-row opening was child-sized, not adult-sized, after sliding the second-row seat. Manuals warn not to adjust seats once restraints are secured, so occupied-seat sliding is not an assumed approved access route. Three-across row-2 use avoids needing that route.

audit.summary: Verified mixed-facing three-across evidence is stronger than a generic three-seat badge, but ANCAP compatibility and the manual’s occupied-seat adjustment warning add important limits. AAA supplies an exact GX observed fuel result. Current used prices and cost anchors remain; repair and aged-service averages are still honest estimates.

items.finding: Used exact-GX Queensland sample remains A$39,990–49,990 drive-away, median A$48,490, n=3, 2021–22, 12,181–106,500 km. Current raw dealer HTML supersedes stale indexed figures. Separately, four new 2025–26 Ingham GX Hybrid VINs are A$64,990–67,250 DAP, median A$64,990; new-stock odometers are unstated. Neither cohort values every grouped year.

2.5L eFour AWD HEV; official 5.6 L/100 km remains distinct from exact 2023 GX AAA observed 5.8 on 95 RON. Manuals verify 288 V/6.5 Ah NiMH, calculated 1.872 kWh nominal; usable capacity unstated. No plug-in charging or electric-only rated range.

Related Grande demonstrates named mixed-facing three-across and 180 cm front clearance. ANCAP found one rear-facing outboard ISOFIX incompatibility. No independent booster-buckle test. Row 3 has no anchors and ANCAP recommends no restraints there. BabyDrive’s occupied-seat sliding observation conflicts with manual warnings against adjustment after installation.

Original launch confirmed five-year unlimited-km private warranty with conditional seven-year engine/driveline cover. Current detailed terms allow annual HEV battery extension to ten years, exclude normal capacity degradation and commercial-use extensions. Balance transfers with vehicle; inspect the original booklet, health checks and delivery date.

Original A$250 eligible annual/15,000 km visits are historical. A$500/year, A$300–700 range, remains an aged-car planning estimate; no VIN-specific post-cap quotation was obtained. Scheduled parts/labour/fluids are included, wear and severe-use additions separate. Original detailed service-book URLs now require login or return unavailable, so plug/coolant/brake-fluid due dates need the car’s logbook.

Insurance rechecked 18 October 2026: A$1,620/year planning budget; A$900–3,200 sensitivity, not guaranteed quotes. NSW GX Hybrid study · annualised five-year cost. No unsupported SUV loading. Your drivers, excess, insured value and cover still need a quote; CTP is separate.

Budget aftermarket audit, 18 October 2026. 235/65R18 106V replacement reference: A$900 for four fitted. Common 40,000 km life is an illustrative assumption, not model-specific wear evidence. Prices and annual savings are estimates; check the real placard and local fitted quote.

Retain A$800/year reserve as savings only; no empirical model-year repair average. AXUH78 pack supplier has no fitted public price, so A$4,500–9,000 replacement scenario remains a weak analogue. Seven relevant campaign topics were checked; latest recliner expansion covers selected production through June 2025 and remedies are free. Verify VIN completion and battery cooling/health records.

ProductReview exact AWD Hybrid page is still 3.0/5 from seven self-selected mixed-grade posts, including one incentive label. Grande wheel-cover/sunroof complaints must not become GX failure rates. The 2022 GX professional test praises refined hybrid driving and roomy seating but criticises dated multimedia; its verdict is Very Good, not a numerical rating.

Braked towing 2,000 kg; cargo 552 L with row 3 folded or 241 L upright. ANCAP 2021 five-star result applies all XU7 variants from March 2021, with curtains covering three rows. Hybrid is four-cylinder QLD fee group: A$864.50–880.50/year including Class 1 CTP at October 2026 rates. Depreciation and repair probability remain estimates; trial seats, pram, parking and VIN service/recall history.
